mechanism_narrative: A rising GDPC1 indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in FEDFUNDS suggests monetary easing, which can boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS drops below 0.05% but S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of next 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases, it signals a strong labor market, which is positive for S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in INDPRO indicates increased production, which can lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low UNRATE indicates a strong labor market, which is positive for equity returns as consumer spending may increase.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains low but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in RSAFS indicates strong consumer demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 grows and FEDFUNDS is low, it indicates strong demand and easy monetary conditions, boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth and low FEDFUNDS but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, decreasing UNRATE and increasing PAYEMS signal a strong economy, positively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 30% of cases.
